[[BPFK_Section: Causation sumtcita#Impact|to'e followed by ki'u, mu'i, ni'i, ri'a or seja'e constitute useful cmavo compounds.]] Here are the complementary explanations with examples.

== Definition of causation sumtcita with to'e and/or nai ==

Causation sumtcita with '''to'e''' and/or '''nai''' are defined along the corresponding causation gismu as follows. The table shows only the case of '''ki'u'''-'''krinu''', but the same correspondence is defined for '''mu'i'''-'''mukti''', '''ni'i'''-'''nibli''', '''ri'a'''-'''rinka''', and '''seja'e'''-'''se jalge'''.

{| class="wikitable" style="width:100%;text-align:left;"
|+ style="text-align:left;"|ki'u
! style="text-align:left;"|di'e panra simxu !! style="text-align:left;"| Corresponding English sentence
|-
| style="font-weight:bold;width:50%;"|<ol><li>ki'u <span style="color:#335ce5;">lo nu broda ku</span> <span style="color:#eb40eb;">brode</span></li>
<li>fi'o krinu <span style="color:#335ce5;">lo nu broda ku</span> <span style="color:#eb40eb;">brode</span></li>
<li><span style="color:#335ce5;">lo nu broda ku</span> krinu <span style="color:#eb40eb;">lo nu brode ku</span></li></ol>
| style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;width:50%;"|<div><span style="color:#335ce5;">Event of broda</span> is reason for <span style="color:#eb40eb;">event of brode</span> (1,2,3).</div>
<div>For the reason that <span style="color:#335ce5;">broda</span>, <span style="color:#eb40eb;">brode</span> is true (1,2).</div>
|}

Examples:
<blockquote>
;ki'u lo nu do cladu ku mi radycru lo nu sipna
:''For the reason of your loud noise, I give up sleeping.''
;lo nu do cladu ku krinu lo nu mi radycru lo nu sipna
:''Your loud noise is reason for my giving up sleeping.''
</blockquote>
'''ki'u''' or any causation sumtcita clause in the scope of '''naku'''-negation may bring little information. See the section [[#Causation sumtcita in the scope of naku-negation|"Causation sumtcita in the scope of '''naku'''-negation"]] for detail.

|+ style="text-align:left;"|ki'u<span style="background-color:#f4fa58;text-decoration:underline;">nai</span>
! style="text-align:left;"|di'e panra simxu !! style="text-align:left;"| Corresponding English sentence
|-
| style="font-weight:bold;width:50%;"|<ol><li>ki'u<span style="background-color:#f4fa58;text-decoration:underline;">nai</span> <span style="color:#335ce5;">lo nu broda ku</span> <span style="color:#eb40eb;">brode</span></li>
<li>fi'o <span style="background-color:#f4fa58;text-decoration:underline;">na'e</span> krinu <span style="color:#335ce5;">lo nu broda ku</span> <span style="color:#eb40eb;">brode</span></li>
<li><span style="color:#335ce5;">lo nu broda ku</span> <span style="background-color:#f4fa58;text-decoration:underline;">na'e</span> krinu <span style="color:#eb40eb;">lo nu brode ku</span></li></ol>
| style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;width:50%;"|<div><span style="color:#335ce5;">Event of broda</span> is <span style="background-color:#f4fa58;text-decoration:underline;">not</span> reason for <span style="color:#eb40eb;">event of brode</span> (1,2,3).</div>
<div><span style="background-color:#f4fa58;text-decoration:underline;">Regardless of</span> <span style="color:#335ce5;">event of broda</span>, <span style="color:#eb40eb;">brode</span> is true (1,2).</div>
|}

Examples:
<blockquote>
;ki'unai lo nu do cladu ku mi radycru lo nu sipna
:''Regardless of your loud noise, I give up sleeping.''
;lo nu do cladu ku na'e krinu lo nu mi radycru lo nu sipna
:''Your loud noise is not reason for my giving up sleeping.''
</blockquote>

{| class="wikitable" style="width:100%;text-align:left;"
|+ style="text-align:left;"|<span style="background-color:#b9e2f7;text-decoration:underline;">to'e</span>ki'u
! style="text-align:left;"|di'e panra simxu !! style="text-align:left;"| Corresponding English sentence
|-
| style="font-weight:bold;width:50%;"|<ol><li><span style="background-color:#b9e2f7;text-decoration:underline;">to'e</span>ki'u <span style="color:#335ce5;">lo nu broda ku</span> <span style="color:#eb40eb;">brode</span></li>
<li>fi'o <span style="background-color:#b9e2f7;text-decoration:underline;">to'e</span> krinu <span style="color:#335ce5;">lo nu broda ku</span> <span style="color:#eb40eb;">brode</span></li>
<li><span style="color:#335ce5;">lo nu broda ku</span> <span style="background-color:#b9e2f7;text-decoration:underline;">to'e</span> krinu <span style="color:#eb40eb;">lo nu brode ku</span></li>
<li><span style="color:#335ce5;">lo nu broda ku</span> krinu <span style="color:#eb40eb;">lo nu <span style="background-color:#b9e2f7;text-decoration:underline;">na</span> brode ku</span></li></ol>
| style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;width:50%;"|<div><span style="color:#335ce5;">Event of broda</span> is reason for <span style="color:#eb40eb;">event of <span style="background-color:#b9e2f7;text-decoration:underline;">not</span> brode</span> (1,2,3,4).</div>
<div><span style="color:#335ce5;">Event of broda</span> <span style="background-color:#b9e2f7;text-decoration:underline;">prevents</span> <span style="color:#eb40eb;">event of brode</span> (1,2,3,4), and <span style="color:#eb40eb;">brode</span> is true (1,2).</div>
|}

Statements 1 and 2 brings unusual meaning, because event of '''brode''' is prevented by event of '''broda''' although '''brode''' is true. For example,
<blockquote>
;to'eki'u lo nu do cladu ku mi radycru lo nu sipna
:''prevented by your loud noise, I give up sleeping.''
:''Your loud noise prevents my giving up sleeping, still I give up sleeping.''
;to'eki'u lo nu do cladu ku mi na sipna
:''prevented by your loud noise, I don't sleep.''
:''Your loud noise prevents my no-sleeping, still I don't sleep.''
</blockquote>
Both statements bring unusual meaning. They seem apparently natural, but pay attention to the scope of '''to'eki'u'''-sumtcita clause<ref name="scope"/>: it spans over the whole statement, and the target of prevention is "my giving up sleeping" and "my no-sleeping" respectively. 

See the section [[#to'e with causation sumtcita in affirmative bridi|"'''to'e''' with causation sumtcita in affirmative bridi"]] for the related discussion.

Reasonable examples:
<blockquote>
;naku mi sipna to'eki'u lo nu do cladu
:''"I sleep prevented by your loud noise" is false.''
</blockquote>
It may be interpreted as ''"I don't sleep"'' or ''"My sleeping is not prevented by your loud noise."'' See the section [[#to'e with causation sumtcita in the scope of naku-negation|'''to'e''' with causation sumtcita in the scope of '''naku'''-negation]] for the related discussion.
<blockquote>
;lo nu do cladu ku krinu lo nu mi na sipna
:''Your loud noise is reason for my non-sleeping.''
:''Your loud noise prevents my sleeping.''
</blockquote>

<li><span style="color:#335ce5;">lo nu broda ku</span> <span style="background-color:#f4fa58;text-decoration:underline;">na'e</span> krinu <span style="color:#eb40eb;">lo nu <span style="background-color:#b9e2f7;text-decoration:underline;">na</span> brode ku</span></li></ol>

<div><span style="color:#335ce5;">Event of broda</span> <span style="background-color:#f4fa58;text-decoration:underline;">does not</span> <span style="background-color:#b9e2f7;text-decoration:underline;">prevent</span> <span style="color:#eb40eb;">event of brode</span> (1,2,3,4), and <span style="color:#eb40eb;">brode</span> is true (1,2).</div>
<div><span style="background-color:#f4fa58;text-decoration:underline;">Des</span><span style="background-color:#b9e2f7;text-decoration:underline;">pite</span> <span style="color:#335ce5;">event of broda</span>, <span style="color:#eb40eb;">brode</span> is true (1,2).</div>
|}

Examples:
<blockquote>
;to'eki'unai lo nu do cladu ku mi sipna
:''Despite your loud noise, I sleep.''
;lo nu do cladu ku na'e krinu lo nu mi na sipna
:''Your loud noise is not reason for my non-sleeping.''
:''Your loud noise does not prevent my sleeping.''
</blockquote>

== Negation of bridi including causation sumtcita ==
=== '''to'e''' with causation sumtcita in affirmative bridi ===
Because "'''to'e'''+causation sumtcita" defined above corresponds to bridi negation of '''brode''', using it in bridi of affirmative '''brode''' may bring unusual meaning. 
<blockquote>
#'''brode to'eki'u lo nu broda'''
#'''brode .i to'eki'u bo broda'''
#'''to'eki'u gi broda gi brode'''
</blockquote>
For the correspondence between these forms, see [[#General note on negation of statements including sumtcita|the section below.]]
Statements 1 and 2 means
<blockquote>
''event of '''broda''' prevents event of '''brode''', still '''brode''' is true.
</blockquote>
If '''brode''' is true, then event of '''brode''' is not prevented by event of '''broda'''!

Statement 3 is rather reasonable, because it does not say whether '''brode''' is true or not.

=== '''to'e''' with causation sumtcita in the scope of '''naku'''-negation ===
Such a paradox does not occur when "'''to'e'''+causation sumtcita" appears <u>in</u> the scope of '''naku'''-negation.
<blockquote>
#'''naku brode to'eki'u lo nu broda'''
#'''naku <u>zo'u</u> brode .i to'eki'u bo broda'''
#'''naku to'eki'u gi broda gi brode'''
</blockquote>
For the correspondence between these forms, see [[#General note on negation of statements including sumtcita|the section below.]]
Statements 1 and 2 may mean:
<blockquote><ol style="list-style-type:lower-greek;">
<li>''Event of '''broda''' prevents event of '''brode''', and '''brode''' is false,'' or</li>
<li>''"Event of '''broda''' prevents event of '''brode'''" is false.''</li>
</ol></blockquote>
Both interpretations are reasonable, though the statements give no further information. According to the interpretation &beta;, it is unclear whether '''brode''' is true or not.

If the speaker intended to mean &alpha;, 
<blockquote>
'''ki'u lo nu broda ku naku brode''' 
</blockquote>
would be more precise. Note that the '''ki'u''' clause is out of the scope of '''naku'''<ref name="scope">The scope in this discussion is the most simple: the preceding &#91;sumtcita/selbri tcita/na(ku)/quantifiers/logical connectives&#93;  span over the following ones. See the pages on [[scope of na]], [[scope of tenses and NA]] and [[scope of selbri tcita]] for further discussions on the scope.</ref>. 

If the speaker intended to mean &beta;, Statement 3 were suitable because it would rejects interpretation &alpha;.
Or, 
<blockquote>
'''naku lo nu broda ku krinu lo nu na brode''' 
</blockquote>
would be also precise. If the speaker intended to mean further that event of '''broda''' and the event of '''brode''' have any non-'''krinu''' relation to each other, then
<blockquote>
'''lo nu broda ku na'e krinu lo nu na brode''' 
</blockquote>
would be more precise. If the speaker intended to mean further that '''brode''' is true,
<blockquote>
'''brode to'eki'unai lo nu broda'''<br/>
''Despite event of '''broda''', '''brode''' is true.''
</blockquote>
would be more precise. Or if the speaker rather intended to mean that '''brode''' is false,
<blockquote>
'''ki'unai lo nu broda ku naku brode'''<br/>
''Regardless of event of '''broda''', '''brode''' is false.''
</blockquote>
would be more precise.
 
=== Causation sumtcita in the scope of '''naku'''-negation ===
Similarly, causation sumtcita without '''to'e''' in the scope of '''naku'''-negation brings little information.
<blockquote>
#'''naku brode ki'u lo nu broda'''
#'''naku <u>zo'u</u> brode .i ki'u bo broda'''
#'''naku ki'u gi broda gi brode'''
</blockquote>
For the correspondence between these forms, see [[#General note on negation of statements including sumtcita|the section below.]]
Statements 1 and 2 may mean:
<blockquote><ol style="list-style-type:lower-greek;">
<li>''Event of '''broda''' is reason for event of '''brode''', and '''brode''' is false,'' or</li>
<li>''"Event of '''broda''' is reason for event of '''brode'''" is false.''</li>
</ol></blockquote>
According to the interpretation &alpha;, the causation is true, but '''brode''' is false, then naturally '''broda''' also should be false.
According to the interpretation &beta;, the causation is false, but it does not say whether '''broda''' or '''brode''' are true or not.
Both interpretations are possible, but the statement gives no further information.

If the speaker intended to mean &alpha;,
<blockquote>
'''ki'u lo nu na broda ku naku brode''' 
</blockquote>
would be more precise. Note that the '''ki'u''' clause is out of the scope of '''naku'''<ref name="scope"/>.

If the speaker intended to mean &beta;, Statement 3 were suitable because it would reject &alpha;.
Or,
<blockquote>
'''naku lo nu broda ku krinu lo nu brode''' 
</blockquote>
would be also precise.


== General note on negation of statements including sumtcita ==
According to [http://lojban.github.io/cll/10/23/ CLL10.23], the following statements correspond to each other:
<blockquote>
'''X BAI lo nu Y'''<br/>
'''X .i BAI bo Y'''<br/>
'''BAI gi Y gi X'''<br/>
<br/>
'''Y PU lo nu X'''<br/>
'''X .i PU bo Y'''<br/>
'''PU gi X gi Y'''
</blockquote>
(PU here means any tense/spatial sumtcita.)

Negation of these statements should be: 
<blockquote>
'''naku X BAI lo nu Y'''<br/>
'''naku <u>zo'u</u> X .i BAI bo Y'''<br/>
'''naku BAI gi Y gi X'''<br/>
<br/>
'''naku Y PU lo nu X'''<br/>
'''naku <u>zo'u</u> X .i PU bo Y'''<br/>
'''naku PU gi X gi Y'''
</blockquote>
Note that '''zo'u''' is required for the form of &#91;'''.i BAI bo'''/'''.i PU bo'''&#93; in order to make '''naku''' span over the whole statement.
